title: Outcome of the battle, Floyd Smith's blues and the band's theme song
summary: Floyd Smith's blues guitar and the popular theme song win the crowd; Pillars wires booking agents including Joe Glaser but nothing happens.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: What was the outcome of the battle with the Sunset Royal?
Well, people -- some people talk about

that now. They respected us from that time on. When they got back up on the bandstand, they were just lost, because -- in fact, everybody in our band had big tones, you know. And they blew those tones out. And we had this little Floyd Smith, and he could play that guitar. And he would play the blues on the guitar, and that's what broke it up.

And our theme song had been popular because we just made it a year before that time. So our theme song was real popular. And when we'd go back up on the bandstand and started playing our theme song, the house just went wild. The house just went wild.
And we had a pretty catchy theme song, too. It was -- well, it was kind of one of the kind of tunes you like to listen to. It had a beautiful sound.

Beautiful sound, beautiful tone, and man, it was pretty, man. It just floated, see. And we stayed there, and our band was a big favorite in Cincinnati, big favorite. And I shall never forget, I sent telegrams to every booking agent that I knew, even Joe Glaser, there's a booking agent in Cleveland, Ohio, see. Because the band was ready. We thought the band was really ready for the big times. And nothing happened. That's life. Timing is -- it plays a most important part in one's life.
